theme: Priestly garments made; the glory fills the Tabernacle
readingInstruction: Read Exodus 39:1-40:38. This reading ends the book of Exodus. The garments are completed, the tabernacle is set up, and the glory of God comes down. Read the last paragraph with particular attention, because it is the goal of the whole book.
settingTheScene: The priestly clothing is finished, and Moses inspects the work. A year after leaving Egypt, on the first day of the first month, the tabernacle is set up (40:17). Each piece is put in its place, and then something happens that no one could have arranged: God’s glory fills the tent. This is the climax of Exodus. The book that began with Israel in slavery ends with God living among his people.
observation: The priestly garments, ephod, breastpiece, robe, and turban, are made “as the LORD had commanded Moses” (39:1, 5, 7, 21, 26, 29, 31).
The plate of the holy crown is engraved “Holy to the LORD” (39:30-31).
Moses inspects the work: “Behold, they had done it; as the LORD had commanded, so had they done it. Then Moses blessed them” (39:43).
The tabernacle is erected on the first day of the first month, in the second year (40:2, 17).
Moses puts the testimony in the ark, sets the mercy seat on top, and brings the ark into the tent (40:20-21).
He anoints the tabernacle and the furniture, and washes and clothes Aaron and his sons (40:9-15, 30-32).

“Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. And Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting because the cloud settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle” (40:34-35).
interpretation:
The last chapter of Exodus echoes the first chapter of Genesis. In Genesis, God makes the world in six days and sees that it is good, and then he blesses it. In Exodus, Moses finishes the tabernacle, looks at the work, and blesses it. The words “So Moses finished the work” (40:33) are almost the same as “Thus the heavens and the earth were finished” (Genesis 2:1). The tabernacle is a new creation, a small world in which God and people may meet.

The date is also significant. The tabernacle is erected on the first day of the first month. It is a new beginning. Israel left Egypt in the month of Passover, and now a year later they have a new center to their life: a sanctuary for the God who brought them out.

Then the glory comes. The same cloud that led them through the wilderness settles on the tent, and God’s presence fills the space so completely that even Moses cannot go in. It is a double lesson. God has come near. And he is still holy. Moses, the friend of God who spoke to him face to face, cannot enter. The nearness of God does not remove his majesty.

The book closes with a description of how the cloud guided Israel. When it lifted, they moved. When it rested, they camped (40:36-38). Their journey was ruled by the presence of God. They did not decide where to go. They followed him. This is the answer to Moses’ prayer in chapter 33, “If your presence will not go with me, do not bring us up from here.” It will go with them, day and night, “in the sight of all the house of Israel throughout all their journeys.”

Exodus began with a groaning people and a hidden God, and it ends with a people who have seen his glory. The book is a short version of the whole Bible: redemption leads to God’s presence. But the story is not finished, because Moses cannot enter. Leviticus will explain how others can.
connection: John says that Jesus “dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory” (John 1:14). At the dedication of Solomon’s temple, the glory fills the house in the same way (1 Kings 8:10-11). Paul says that believers are God’s temple (1 Corinthians 3:16), and Revelation shows the glory of God filling the new Jerusalem so that it has no need of the sun (Revelation 21:23).
application:
Reflect on the end of Exodus. God rescued his people so that he could live with them. Thank him that this is the goal of your salvation, and not only forgiveness.

Ask yourself how much of your life is guided by his presence, and how much by your own plans.

Spend a few quiet minutes asking God to fill your life with his glory.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that his glory fills his church.
Ask him to lead you day by day.
Ask him to let his presence rule your journey.
